motivation: The exact-point recovery analyses show that Thalassia is frequently re-recorded after a one-year loss. Test whether such returns are stable or more fragile than uninterrupted occupancy.

four_year_sequence.years: t, t+1, t+2, t+3 observed consecutively at the same stable meter mark
four_year_sequence.recovered_group: Thalassia present at t, absent at t+1, present at t+2
four_year_sequence.continuous_group: Thalassia present at t, t+1, and t+2
four_year_sequence.note: Because t >= 2016, recovered-group loss years begin in 2017; the independently protocol-sensitive 2016 loss year is excluded structurally.

primary_hypothesis.statement: Exact-point Thalassia returns after a one-year loss are more likely to be followed by another recorded loss than continuously occupied meter marks.
primary_hypothesis.model: L2 logistic regression for t+3 recorded loss
primary_hypothesis.estimator: coefficient for recovered_group after stable-node and return-year adjustment
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for recovered_group coefficient > 0

secondary: raw recorded re-loss fraction in recovered and continuous groups

interpretation.supported: Re-recorded Thalassia after a one-year exact-point loss is a more fragile state than uninterrupted occupancy, consistent with hysteresis or incomplete local recovery.
interpretation.unsupported: Returned points are not detectably more fragile than continuously occupied points at the next annual observation; re-recording appears comparably stable at this temporal resolution.

claim_boundary: Recorded re-loss is an observation-state transition, not demographic relapse or mortality.
A fragility effect could reflect patchiness, detectability, residual local stress, or demographic instability; it does not identify the mechanism.
Continuous controls are adjusted for stable node and return year but are not experimentally matched.
Do not alter the four-year state patterns, period, comparison group, model, minima, or support threshold after opening t+3 states.
